newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian sorghum seen steady - Grainco.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian sorghum seen steady - Grainco.

text.p: Australia's southern Queensland sorghum market continues to show minimal nearby grower selling, with harvest almost complete in most areas, Rob Brealey, trading manager of state co-operative Grainco, said in a weekly review.

Prices were likely to remain steady to slightly stronger, he said. Central Queensland's spring sorghum harvest continued to progress slowly amid wet weather, but lack of domestic demand in the short-term continues to keep values steady, he said.
Domestic values finished last week around A$146.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane for March.

Australia's feed barley market continues quiet with only limited tonnage traded over the past week in the low to mid A$130.00 a tonne range on farm in southern Queensland and northern New South Wales.
Australian production could be less than last season, particularly as areas in the southern states continue dry.
Parts of Victoria and South Australia in particular will need planting rain over the next three to four weeks, he said.
While this was likely to favour malting rather than feed values, it could still support feed values in the longer-term, Brealey said.
Domestic values remain steady with Grainco's malting barley cash bid finishing last week steady at A$170.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane.
Little if any old crop malting barley remains uncommitted.
Enquiries and trade in the cottonseed market picked up over the past week from both domestic and export markets, Brealey said.

The cotton crop is expected by most to be about 2.4 million bales, which should produce 750,000 tonnes to 775,000 tonnes of seed. This should tend to support the market from significant price pressure, he said.
Ginning pressure and seed from a record crop may cause some price weakness, although cottonseed is competitively valued with grain prices strengthening recently, Brealey said.
Despite the liklihood of a reduction in domestic consumption, domestic users are now looking to cover base requirements. Similarly, export consumers see seed at current levels as fair value, he said.
With existing old crop stocks now run down and purchases for the new crop limited, export consumers are moving to secure coverage for the April to September periods.

Cottonseed prices have strengthened as a result of increased activity. Cash prices last week traded between A$125.00 and A$130.00 a tonne across Queensland gins to growers. The price outlook remains stable at current levels.
Australian oilseeds values remained steady over the past week with sunflowers finishing at A$310.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane.
New crop soybean prices were firmer at A$408.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane while canola was lower at A$340.00 a tonne delivered Moree for March.
